doc: Gate datasets. Fields: id (also the name of the reference file), corpus (an id in benchmarks/corpus/registry.json), target (a column name, "@last" for the last column, or omitted), components (names; omitted means all registered components), held_out (scored and written to the scorecard, reported apart, excluded from the pass/fail comparison by default), fast (member of the --fast subset), read (overrides of the corpus read options, for example parse_dates), hints and detectors (passed to profile; hints default to the corpus entry's), options ({component: {option: value}}, for example {"planted": {"plants": ["sum_identity"]}}). The headline list names the metrics report.py shows first, each with a column label and a one-line meaning. See benchmarks/gate/README.md.

headline.label: planted found in 4k digest
headline.meaning: known structures injected into real tables that the 4,000-character digest states

headline.label: must statements in 4k digest
headline.meaning: hand-written reference statements of tier must that the digest states, default mode

headline.label: must statements in 4k digest, target mode
headline.meaning: the same count with the dataset's target designated

headline.label: statements on shuffled tables (4k digest)
headline.meaning: relationship statements in the digest of a table whose columns were shuffled independently, where no relationship exists

headline.label: facts changed by layout
headline.meaning: stated facts lost or gained when columns are reordered, rows shuffled, columns renamed, a noise column added, or a column rescaled

headline.label: repeated facts in 4k digest
headline.meaning: digest lines that restate the columns and relation of an earlier line

headline.label: statement mismatches
headline.meaning: statements whose recount against the data disagrees with the report
